content.title: Scan Business Card to Contacts on iPhone
content.meta_description: Scan paper business cards with your iPhone camera to instantly recognise names, phones, and emails and create reviewed iOS Contacts.
content.h1: How to Scan a Business Card Directly to iPhone Contacts
content.quick_answer: To scan a business card into iPhone Contacts, point your camera at the card using a scanner app with business card recognition. The app uses on-device OCR to extract the name, company, phone number, email address, and physical address, letting you review and edit the details before saving the new contact directly to iOS.
intro: Returning from an industry conference with a stack of twenty paper business cards often leads to an evening of tedious typing. Manually keying names, phone numbers, and job titles into an iPhone address book takes time and invites typos.

Using an iPhone camera to digitise cards streamlines the process. This guide covers how to capture cards, extract contact fields automatically with on-device recognition, verify the information, and save records straight into Apple Contacts.

If you instead need to save expense slips, see our guide on how to scan receipts on iPhone. For general full-page text extraction, read about converting scanned images to text, or explore how to scan documents without an app.
content.steps_heading: Steps to Scan a Business Card into iOS Contacts

steps.title: Position the card in good light
steps.detail: Place the business card flat on a contrasting surface so the edges stand out. Ensure light is even across the card to prevent reflections on glossy paper from obscuring fine text.

steps.title: Capture the card using Business Card mode
steps.detail: Open Document Scanner & PDF Toolkit and choose the business card tool. Hold your iPhone steady over the card; automatic edge detection will identify the borders, crop the view, and straighten the perspective.

steps.title: Allow on-device OCR to read the text
steps.detail: The app reads the printed text locally on your iPhone. It categorises the detected text lines into standard fields: name, company, phone number, email, and address.

steps.title: Review the details before saving
steps.detail: Inspect the populated contact card on your screen. Check that unusual job titles or stylized company logos were not confused with names, and make any quick edits before tapping to save the entry directly into your iOS Contacts.

content.alternatives_heading: Alternative Ways to Add Contacts from Paper Cards

alternatives.method: Apple Live Text in the Camera or Photos app
alternatives.how: Point your iPhone Camera at the card on iOS 15 or later. Tap the Live Text icon when it appears, tap the detected phone number or email address, and select the prompt to add it to your contacts.
alternatives.best_for: Adding a single phone number or email address quickly without installing an app.
alternatives.limitation: Live Text detects individual data strings rather than creating a complete contact record in one tap, requiring you to copy and paste names, titles, and addresses separately.

alternatives.method: Manual entry into the iOS Contacts app
alternatives.how: Open the native Contacts app on your iPhone, tap the plus icon, and type the name, company, phone number, and email address by hand from the paper card.
alternatives.best_for: Cards with artistic fonts, vertical text layouts, or embossed logos that optical readers struggle to decipher.
alternatives.limitation: It is slow, repetitive, and prone to typographical errors when processing multiple cards from events.

content.features_heading: Core Scanning Features for Business Cards

feature_points.benefit: Extracts the contact's name, company, phone number, email, and physical address automatically and generates a ready-to-review iOS contact card.
Finds the small borders of standard cards instantly, cropping out table backgrounds and correcting slight angles.
Extracts printed contact details directly on the iPhone with high accuracy, without requiring manual transcription.
Ensures personal contact data, phone numbers, and corporate emails never leave your phone, keeping client records private.

content.tips_heading: Tips for Accurately Scanning Business Cards
tips: Use a dark, non-reflective background when capturing white or light-coloured cards to ensure automatic edge detection crops cleanly.
Watch out for glare from overhead lights on glossy finishes or metallic foil lettering, as reflections can cause OCR reading errors.
Always verify phone country codes and extension numbers, as unconventional formatting on modern cards may require minor manual adjustment.
If a card features text on both sides, check the back for direct extension numbers or secondary addresses before filing the paper away.

faqs.question: How do I scan a business card directly into Apple Contacts?
faqs.answer: Using Document Scanner & PDF Toolkit, capture the card using the business card feature. The app reads the card's printed information, maps it into a new iOS contact card, and lets you save it directly to your address book after a brief review.

faqs.question: Which contact fields does the scanner recognise automatically?
faqs.answer: The on-device OCR tool identifies the person's name, company name, telephone numbers, email address, and street address printed on the card.

faqs.question: Can I review and edit the contact details before saving them to iOS Contacts?
faqs.answer: Yes. After the card is scanned, the app displays the extracted information in editable fields. You can correct typos, adjust names, or add notes before committing the record to your device's Contacts.

faqs.question: How can I use iOS Live Text to add a phone number or email from a card?
faqs.answer: On an iPhone XS/XR or newer running iOS 15 or later, open the native Camera app and point it at the business card. When the Live Text indicator highlights the text, tap the phone number or email address, then tap Add to Contacts in the action menu.

faqs.question: Are business card details processed on my iPhone or sent to a server?
faqs.answer: All scanning and text recognition tasks run locally on your device. Your captured cards and newly created contacts are never uploaded to an external server.
